title: Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018
short_title: Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require tobacco importers to pay import duty on tobacco products at the time they are brought into Australia, rather than when they leave a warehouse.

It would amend the Customs Act 1901 to end the option of storing imported tobacco in a licensed warehouse without paying duty, and to stop weekly or monthly duty payment arrangements from 1 July 2019.

Owners of tobacco still in warehouses on 1 July 2019 must enter the goods for home consumption and pay outstanding duty, or arrange to pay over 12 months with a security, or risk having the tobacco sold or disposed of by the government.
changes: Requires import duty on tobacco to be paid upon importation into Australia from 1 July 2019.
Removes the option to enter imported tobacco into a licensed warehouse without paying duty from 1 July 2019.
Ends weekly or monthly duty payment permissions under section 69 of the Customs Act from 1 July 2019.
Ceases movement permissions for tobacco to or from warehouses from 1 July 2019.
Imposes transitional arrangements for tobacco in warehouses on 1 July 2019, requiring owners to pay duty or arrange payment over 12 months with a security.
Exempts tobacco in duty free stores or warehouses used for aircraft or ship stores from the transitional arrangements.
summary.affected: Tobacco importers and owners of tobacco products in warehouses.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The government introduced the Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill, requiring tobacco importers to pay all duties upon importation from 1 July 2019, ending the option to defer payment via licensed warehouses, to combat the illicit tobacco black market and raise an estimated $3.3 billion in revenue.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018 requires tobacco importers to pay duty upon importation from 1 July 2019, closing a warehouse loophole for illicit tobacco. The speaker argued this change also generates a one-off $3.27 billion revenue boost in 2019-20, allowing the government to claim a budget surplus a year earlier than otherwise possible.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speech concerned the Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018, and noted that Labor's last budget surplus was in 1989, approaching its 30th anniversary, in contrast to the member for Blair's remarks on surpluses.

speeches.speaker: Tim Wilson
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018, arguing it simplifies duty collection and secures government revenue. They criticised plain packaging and tax increases for driving counterfeit markets, and advocated for legal access to vaping as a harm reduction measure, citing examples from the UK and US.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018 will require importers to pay all tobacco duties at the border from 1 July 2019, aiming to prevent criminal groups from accessing duty-free tobacco. The bill is part of a package with two other bills targeting tobacco duty collection at manufacture.
